summary: Tajikistan's Consular Department says that from 1 January 2022 the country introduced a unilateral visa-free system allowing citizens of 52 countries to enter and stay for 30 days; its country table lists, among others, the United States, Canada, Australia, Japan, Germany and France as visa-free for up to 30 days, and Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Ukraine and Georgia as visa-free indefinitely. Electronic visas are applied for on evisa.tj, with an optional permit to enter GBAO selected on the same form, and visas can also be applied for at a Tajik diplomatic mission or consular post. The UK government tells British nationals they must have a visa and to apply online for an e-visa before travelling.

currencyLimits.text: The UK Foreign Office says travellers may bring up to USD 10,000 (or the equivalent) into Tajikistan without declaring it, that any amount exceeding this should be declared before entry, that above USD 10,000 travellers must present documents confirming the origin of the funds, and that up to USD 3,000 (or the equivalent) can be taken out without a declaration. It recommends keeping your entry declaration form until departure.

notes: The UK says customs declaration forms are available in Russian and English, recommends keeping your entry declaration form until departure to prove how much money you brought in, and says failure to declare or provide documentation may result in fines or delays at the border.

The UK says the possession or use of drones is prohibited unless you have permission from the Tajik National Security Committee, and that without it you may be detained and your equipment confiscated.

Australia's Smartraveller says some medications, including codeine, are restricted in Tajikistan: confirm yours are legal, and declare all medicines and other restricted items on arrival, or you could face charges.

payments.text: The UK says Tajikistan is mainly a cash-only economy where very few businesses accept credit cards. It says ATMs are increasingly common in Dushanbe and other larger towns but there are none in rural areas, and most accept only Visa cards. US dollars are the most easily exchanged foreign currency, but official exchange booths may not accept damaged or marked notes, nor US dollars issued before 2013.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says pickpocketing is common in crowded places such as markets and on public transport and that terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Tajikistan; Canada's travel advice says the land border between Tajikistan and Afghanistan has been closed since the Taliban takeover in 2021.

tips.text: The UK government says you need a separate travel permit, in addition to a Tajik visa, for the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO); Canada and Australia also say a permit or pre-authorization is needed. E-visa applicants select it on the same electronic-visa form; the UK says others can apply through the Tajik Embassy before travelling or, in Tajikistan, through the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The UK government says you must get a permit, in addition to a Tajik visa, to travel to areas within 20km of the border with Afghanistan in the Khatlon Region, applied for at the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dushanbe, and that the Tajikistan government sometimes stops issuing GBAO permits to tourists at short notice due to security concerns.

The UK advises bringing enough cash for your entire stay or withdrawing cash from an ATM in Dushanbe before travelling to other regions. It says very few businesses accept credit cards, there are no ATMs in rural areas, and official exchange booths may not accept damaged or marked notes, nor US dollars issued before 2013.

Tajikistan's Consular Department says citizens of the 52 visa-free countries must register with the relevant authorities within 10 working days of entry, and that holders of an electronic visa are exempt from registration. The UK government says hotels are no longer permitted to register guests, and that those entering without an e-visa and staying longer than 10 days must register with the OVIR office in Dushanbe.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tajikistan?
faq.answer: Tajikistan's Consular Department lists, among others, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Germany and France as visa-free for up to 30 days, and Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Ukraine and Georgia as visa-free indefinitely. The UK government tells British nationals they must have a visa and to apply online for an e-visa before travelling. Electronic visas are applied for on evisa.tj, and visas can also be applied for at a Tajik diplomatic mission or consular post.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Tajikistan?
faq.answer: No. Tajikistan's Consular Department lists the United States as visa-free for up to 30 days. It says foreign citizens entering for more than 30 days for employment, education, permanent residence and other purposes must have a visa suitable for the purpose of the trip before travelling.

faq.question: What is the GBAO permit and when do I need it?
faq.answer: The UK government says you must get a separate travel permit, in addition to a Tajik visa, to travel to the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region; Canada and Australia also say you need a permit or pre-authorization. On the e-visa, the permit is selected on the electronic-visa form and costs USD 20. The UK says that if you're in the UK you should contact the Tajik Embassy to apply before you travel, and if you're in Tajikistan, the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

faq.question: How much does the Tajikistan eVisa cost and how long does it take?
faq.answer: Tajikistan's consular fee table sets USD 30 for considering a single-entry e-visa application for up to 60 days and USD 50 for multiple entry during a period of up to 60 days; the permit to enter GBAO is USD 20. The Consular Department says the e-visa is valid for 90 days, but the holder may stay no more than 60 calendar days. Apply at evisa.tj. No official source we could read states a processing time.

faq.question: Can I enter Tajikistan overland with an eVisa?
faq.answer: Tajikistan's e-visa portal says e-visa holders can enter the Republic of Tajikistan through all border points. Canada's travel advice says the land border between Tajikistan and Afghanistan has been closed since the Taliban takeover in 2021.

tips.border-status.text: You must get a permit, in addition to a Tajik visa, to travel to areas within 20km of the border with Afghanistan in the Khatlon Region, including Panj and Kumsangir. Apply for a permit from the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dushanbe before you travel to the Khatlon region.
The Tajikistan government sometimes stops issuing permits to tourists at short notice due to security concerns.

tips.cash-usd.text: Bring enough cash for your entire stay or withdraw cash from an ATM in Dushanbe ahead of any planned travel to other regions.
Very few businesses accept credit cards and travellers’ cheques are not accepted. There is an increasing number of ATMs in Dushanbe and other larger towns, but none in rural areas.
Official exchange booths may not accept damaged or marked bank notes, nor will they accept US dollars issued before 2013.

tips.registration.text: However, citizens of 52 foreign countries are obliged to register in the relevant authorities of the country within 10 working days from the date of their entry into the Republic of Tajikistan and leave the Republic of Tajikistan after the expiration of their 30-day stay.
Foreign citizens who hold an electronic visa are exempt from registration with the internal-affairs authorities of the Republic of Tajikistan.

If you are entering Tajikistan without an e-visa and staying for longer than 10 days, you must register with the Office for Registration of Foreign Citizens (OVIR) located at 5 Mirzo Tursunzoda Street, Dushanbe. Hotels are no longer permitted to complete the registration on your behalf.

entryRequirements.passportValidity.text: As a rule, the passport must not expire earlier than 6 months before the visa expires. The document must have at least 2 blank pages reserved for a visa.
To enter Tajikistan, your passport must have an ‘expiry date’ at least 6 months after the date you arrive and have at least 2 blank pages.

entryRequirements.customs.currencyLimits.text: Travellers may bring up to $10,000 US dollars (or equivalent in other currencies) into Tajikistan without declaring it at customs. Any amount exceeding this should be declared before entry. Travellers may take up to $3,000 US dollars (or equivalent) out of the country without declaration. If the amount exceeds $10,000 US dollars, travellers must present documentation confirming the origin of the funds.
It is recommended to retain your entry declaration form until departure to prove the amount of money originally brought into the country.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.0.text: Customs declaration forms are available in Russian and English. It is recommended to retain your entry declaration form until departure to prove the amount of money originally brought into the country. Failure to declare or provide documentation may result in fines or delays at the border.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.1.text: The possession or use of drones or UAVs is prohibited unless you have permission from the Tajik National Security Committee. If you are found using drones without permission, you may be detained and your equipment confiscated.

entryRequirements.customs.notes.2.text: Some medications including codeine are restricted in Tajikistan. If you intend to bring medication on your travels, confirm it's legal and check the rules that apply. Declare all medicines and other restricted items on arrival. If you don't, or if the amount you carry is over the legal limits, you could face charges.

countryFacts.payments.text: Tajikistan is mainly a cash-only economy. Very few businesses accept credit cards and travellers’ cheques are not accepted. There is an increasing number of ATMs in Dushanbe and other larger towns, but none in rural areas. Most ATMs only accept Visa cards.
US dollars are the most easily exchanged and widely accepted foreign currency.
Official exchange booths may not accept damaged or marked bank notes, nor will they accept US dollars issued before 2013.

countryFacts.safety.text: Pickpocketing is common in crowded places such as markets and on public transport.
Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Tajikistan.
The land border between Tajikistan and Afghanistan has been closed since the Taliban takeover in 2021.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: In Tajikistan, the rainy season usually extends from January to May and from October to December. Rainfall is rare during summer months.
Many interior roads are only open in the summer months.

countryFacts.driving.text: You are permitted to drive in Tajikistan with a valid UK driving licence for up to 30 days. In addition, you must carry the 1968 version of the International Driving Permit (IDP) alongside your UK licence:
